Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things. It's been a challenge for her, especially when trying to read or watch TV. We're really worried about how this might affect her learning.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had fluid in her ear for a while, and we were so scared it would affect her hearing permanently. Luckily, after treatment, everything seems back to normal now. But I still get anxious whenever she complains about her ear.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been an issue for her since she started eating solid foods. Some foods are just too hard for her to manage. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make sure she can eat comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says she needs regular check-ups to monitor her heart health. I try to stay on top of these appointments because I know how crucial they are for her well-being. It's always a relief when the results come back normal.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower than her peers to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. It was worrying at first, but with therapy and support, she's making progress. I'm just eager for her to catch up.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures can be a real issue for her. She's very picky and will only eat certain things if they're prepared in specific ways. Mealtime can be challenging, but we're learning to navigate her preferences.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... two main concerns. Firstly, her fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely. And secondly, her speech development isn't where it should be for her age. She doesn't speak as much as other children her age. Both these things worry me and I hope we can find ways to support her better.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart checks to monitor her heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences food textures as a challenge, being very picky and only eating certain things if they are prepared in specific ways.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower than peers to reach certain milestones, but with therapy and support, she is making progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have brain-related issues, including cognitive delays and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely, and she has experienced challenges with her speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have craniofacial abnormalities, including a triangular-shaped face, wide-spaced eyes, and thick eyebrows that sometimes join in the center.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things, and she has had fluid in her ear, requiring treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, squint, and hearing loss.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences chewing difficulties due to her large permanent teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and difficulty managing food textures.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower than peers to reach certain milestones, but with therapy and support, she is making progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have developmental delays and behavioral differences, and around 38% have cognitive delays.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower than peers to reach certain milestones, and her speech development is not where it should be for her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has brachydactylous fingers and a curved 5th finger, and some have had hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have skeletal abnormalities, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones, shortened fingers, and hips that can be easily dislocated.

d) Feeding assistance: The patient has been slow to develop certain milestones and requires mealtime adjustments to accommodate her preferences.

Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups to monitor and ensure proper heart function.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences slower weight gain compared to peers, suggesting potential issues with digestion or nutrient absorption.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are distressing for him and his family.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and these episodes can be challenging for both the patient and their caregivers.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the volume of the TV up very high to hear it clearly, suggesting he might be experiencing hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision, particularly when watching TV or reading, indicating possible hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has chewing difficulties with hard foods, suggesting potential issues with tooth strength or jaw function.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and should brush their teeth regularly.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires extra help in school, especially in areas such as playing with toys, using cutlery, and toilet training.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and these episodes can be challenging for both the patient and their caregivers.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and some have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A small number of children have had hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires monitoring by the cardiologist to prevent any major issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with mealtimes, getting constipated or having loose stools, and working with a dietitian to find the right balance of foods that agree with her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, requiring ongoing monitoring by the neurologists to assess potential effects on development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced a delayed fontanelle closure and has shorter-than-average fingers, both of which are being monitored as the patient grows and develops.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness, with occasional squinting and strabismus.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness, with occasional squinting and strabismus.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, making her teeth more susceptible to cavities and sensitivity, and she makes sure to brush them carefully and limits sugary foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient attends a mainstream primary school with additional help needed, and some go to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication may be appropriate in some circumstances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has brachydactylous fingers with a curvature of the 5th finger, and a small number of children have had hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening for heart abnormalities: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires monitoring by the cardiologist.
b) Monitoring for tethered cord: The patient has a tethered cord, requiring ongoing monitoring by the neurologists to assess potential effects on development.
c) Feeding difficulties: The patient experiences challenges with mealtimes, getting constipated or having loose stools, and working with a dietitian to find the right balance of foods that agree with her.
d) Dental care: The patient has weak enamel, making her teeth more susceptible to cavities and sensitivity, and she makes sure to brush them carefully and limits sugary foods and drinks.
